We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 1 & 1 & -4 & 7 \\  & ↓ & 1 & -3 \\  & 1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-4x+7}{x-1}=x-3+\frac{4}{x-1}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}-4x+7}{x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (x-3+\frac{4}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int x\,\text{d}x-3\int \text{d}x+4\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-3x+4\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$
